title: ChatWire: OpenAI ChatCompletions protocol translation adapter
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Implement a lightweight translation adapter (internally: ChatWire) that maps Redwood inference requests/responses to/from the OpenAI Chat Completions API semantics. The adapter should preserve streaming semantics, support function/tool calling and structured output modes, and provide deterministic mappings for finish reasons, tokens, and error cases so Redwood-hosted customers can use OpenAI-compatible clients with minimal changes.
motivation: Customers and partner integrations often expect OpenAI ChatCompletions wire semantics. We need a compatibility layer that avoids requiring client-side changes while keeping Redwood runtime optimizations (batching, KV cache) and observability intact. This reduces migration friction and allows Redwood to accept previously built integrations and third-party tooling that speak OpenAI semantics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Functional parity: For a representative suite of prompts (chat, system instructions, assistant messages), the adapter returns semantically equivalent content compared to direct OpenAI responses (modulo allowed randomness).
2) Streaming parity: Clients that consume OpenAI-style SSE streams receive equivalent event order, delta payloads, and final finish_reason mapping when routed through ChatWire.

3) Function/tool calling: OpenAI-style function_call invoked by the model maps to Redwood tool invocation surface with preserved function name and streamed/complete arguments; client-visible deltas align with OpenAI behavior.

4) Structured output: JSON-schema/response_format style requests are returned consistently; when model returns malformed JSON the adapter emits the same error/finish semantics OpenAI clients expect (plus telemetry tags).

5) Testing & monitoring: End-to-end tests cover 200+ prompt variations, streaming integration tests run in CI, and dashboards surface adapter translation failures and mismatch rates <0.5% in first month after rollout.
6) Backward compatibility: Existing Redwood routes continue to work; ChatWire must be opt-in via compatibility flag and revertible via config toggle.
proposal: Add a protocol translation layer between the Redwood API layer and the runtime request pipeline. The adapter has two responsibilities: (A) inbound mapping: translate OpenAI-style client requests into Redwood internal request objects (preserving role/message semantics, function definitions, and streaming flags), and (B) outbound mapping: translate Redwood runtime responses and stream events back into OpenAI-style messages/events. The adapter does not change model selection nor runtime kernel choices — it only mutates request/response envelopes and augments telemetry.
api_mapping: Inbound: map OpenAI 'messages' array to Redwood message records. Roles map directly (system/user/assistant); unknown roles map to 'user' with a warning tag. Map OpenAI 'functions' array -> Redwood 'tools' descriptors (name, description, parameters JSON Schema). Map 'function_call' hint (none/auto/string) to Redwood tool invocation hint. Map top-level params (temperature,max_tokens,stop,stream) to Redwood request options with defined caps. Outbound: map Redwood choice objects -> OpenAI choices array. Normalize finish_reason ('stop','length','function_call','content_filter','error') to OpenAI finish_reason strings; include 'index' ordering and delta content chunks for streaming. Include 'usage' token counts in OpenAI-compatible structure.
streaming_mapping: Redwood uses framed delta events internally; ChatWire will emit SSE events matching OpenAI streaming shapes. Key behaviors: 1) Emit partial 'delta' objects with nested 'content' or 'function_call' deltas as OpenAI does. 2) For function_call streaming: emit name first (when available) and stream 'arguments' as successive deltas following OpenAI delta conventions. 3) Ensure the final SSE 'data: [DONE]' aligns with OpenAI's timing and contains final aggregated content in the last chunk if the client expects it. 4) Preserve token-level timing where possible but cap batch aggregation to avoid excessive event count. 5) Provide a non-streaming fallback that returns identical final payload shape as OpenAI synchronous completions.
function_call_mapping: Two modes: 1) Passive mapping (compatibility only): when model suggests a function_call in Redwood internal response, translate to OpenAI 'choices[0].finish_reason':'function_call' and include 'message':{'role':'assistant','content':null,'function_call':{'name':..., 'arguments':...}}. 2) Active tool invocation: if Redwood is configured to actually run tools, ChatWire should invoke the matched tool, capture the tool's result, and return a second assistant message with role 'tool' or as OpenAI would expect. Streaming tool outputs should be chunked as function_call 'arguments' deltas followed by tool result as assistant content. Decision: default behaviour is passive mapping unless route-level config enables automatic tool execution.
structured_output_mapping: Support two common patterns: 'response_format' hints (JSON/JSON_SCHEMA) and OpenAI 'functions' with 'parameters' schema. For JSON_SCHEMA prompts we set a strict post-processing validator in the adapter: if model output fails validation, adapter will attach a 'validation_error' field to the returned metadata and, when possible, attempt a safe tidying pass using a lightweight deterministic reparsing step (limit to 1 retry). This mirrors common OpenAI client recommendations while exposing validation failures in telemetry. Also include an optional 'raw_output' field in logs for debugging (access-controlled).
error_handling: Map Redwood runtime errors to OpenAI-compatible HTTP statuses and bodies. Examples: model not available -> 503 with code 'model_not_available'; rate limit -> 429 with 'rate_limit' and retry-after header; content filter -> 400 with 'content_filter' finish_reason. Streaming errors: send a final SSE error event that mirrors OpenAI streaming termination patterns and include a machine-readable 'x-redwood-adapter-error' tag. Ensure internal error types are logged with correlation IDs and surfaced to console error dashboards.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gating: behind 'compat.chatwire' feature flag at route level; default off.
2) Canary: enable for 5% of eligible hosted customers and all internal test orgs for 48 hours.
3) Metrics: monitor mismatch-rate, client error increase, latency p50/p95 difference, streaming event rate, function_call success rate.
4) Ramp: if metrics stable, 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
5) Rollback: immediate toggle off; automated rollback if mismatch-rate > 1% or error rate > baseline + 0.5%.
6) Communication: announce to partners with migration notes and opt-in SDK helper.
7) Postmortem: 30-day review and adapt default behavior (passive vs active tool invocation).
testing: Unit tests for inbound/outbound mapping functions (message roles, function schemas, finish_reason).
Integration tests that diff direct-OpenAI vs ChatWire responses for a representative corpus (streaming and non-streaming).
Streaming contract tests that assert event ordering, delta shapes, and SSE boundaries.
Tool-call simulation tests (mocked tool execution and streamed arguments).
Load tests to ensure adapter does not add >5% p95 latency overhead under typical traffic patterns.
links: Related tickets: ENG-27102 (streaming infra), ENG-26988 (tooling contract)
notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) We could choose to always execute functions server-side for a nicer out-of-the-box UX, but this increases security surface and coupling to tools — defaulting to passive mapping reduces risk. 2) Aggressive event aggregation reduces SSE pressure but slightly changes client-observed token boundaries; we opt for configurable aggregation thresholds. Ops: enable verbose adapter-level logs for first week after rollout and purge raw outputs after 30 days to reduce PII risks. Security review required because adapter surfaces tool schemas and may change execution semantics.
